method: End-to-end UI verification at mobile CSS viewport sizes, using employee and manager demonstration accounts
checks: All filter displays 11 notifications; unread filter displays exactly 7 initially
Explicitly marking JP-1004 creation notification read reduces unread count and list length from 7 to 6 without navigating away
Opening JP-1003 creation notification displays the correct request and its current approved status and history
Returning from request preserves unread filter; opening notification reduces unread count to 5
Opening welcome-course assignment notification displays the correct course and reduces unread count to 4
Returning from course preserves the unread filter; merely opening course leaves learning progress unchanged
All filter retains read notifications; total remains 11
Mark-all-read reduces unread count to zero, empties unread filter and displays confirmation
Empty unread filter shows explanatory text and a button to show all notifications
Show-all button returns all 11 cards; all individual read buttons disappear and mark-all-read is disabled
Header badge clears when unread count is zero
All 11 read flags persist after reload and after logout/login
Previously read completion notification opens saved course result with 80% and does not change count or create duplicate notifications
Manager still has its own 4 unread request notifications after employee marks all read
Mobile cards, filters and actions fit viewport; at 360px page clientWidth and scrollWidth both equal 345px
reason: No functional or layout defect found in verified notification scenarios
limits: Responsive browser verification, not a physical iOS/Android device test
cleanup: Viewport reset; employee notifications intentionally left read following the bulk-read test
